name: Baguette
role: Apple Simulator control and capture CLI with multi-device orchestration
notes: 2026-11-15: Triage: assess; scripted simulator gestures and capture fill a distinct native-app preview route. Revisit if supported macOS/Xcode requirements exceed the target environment or capture cannot be repeated reliably.
2026-11-24: Guide written from examples/baguette-simulator-capture; tested 0.3.2 (assessment saw 0.2.14), one iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.5 sim on macOS 26.6 arm64.
2026-11-15: Skill opportunity: consider a VCR simulator-capture guide if this becomes a recurring app-capture workflow; assess Xcode and host constraints in a scoped fixture.

evidence.result: Booted iPhone 17 Pro (EN) iOS 26.5 by UDID, took a 1206x2622 PNG screenshot and a 3 s H.264 MP4 of a home-screen swipe (duration 3.007 s; 42 frames), frames non-blank and different, device Shutdown afterwards. Final record and verify runs both OK. ffprobe 9.0.2, ImageMagick 7.1.2, macOS 26.6 arm64.
evidence.scope: Boot one named iPhone 17 Pro (EN) iOS 26.5 sim by UDID; PNG and 3 s home-screen H.264 capture at 1206x2622, shutdown; no pixel hashes or input latency; macOS arm64 only

summary: Native macOS CLI for headless Apple Simulator control, screenshots, video recording, UI descriptions and multi-device sessions. Its broad simulator input and capture commands make it useful for repeatable app capture; it requires Apple Silicon and Xcode 26 private simulator frameworks.
use_when: Automate taps, gestures and screenshots in Apple Simulator without driving the GUI
Record or stream simulator sessions alongside scripted UI input
Coordinate multiple simulator devices from a CLI
avoid_when: Use XCUITest when you need Apple’s supported test framework and assertions
Use iOS Simulator UI automation when accessibility-driven app interaction is sufficient

assessment.rationale: Official docs describe a native CLI for Apple Simulator control, recording and multi-device sessions; v0.2.14 was released 2026-11-07. Install requires Apple Silicon, Xcode 26 and private SimulatorKit/CoreSimulator frameworks, so portability is limited.
